harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a Kea DHCPv4 server on the private network (eth1/enp8s0, 10.50.50.0/24) shared with node2 and node3, and configured node2/node3 to obtain their address on that network via DHCP (systemd-networkd) instead of static assignment. Implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4, the pre-provisioned Ansible control node. Bootstrapped SSH access from node4 to node1 (vyos user, via VyOS's own config-managed public-keys so it survives reboots) and to node2/node3 (root; had to generate missing SSH host keys and enable the disabled sshd service). All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via native reboot, with boot-id-based proof of restart and post-restart verification that DHCP server config and client leases fully recovered. A final full playbook re-run after all restarts confirmed idempotency and correctness of the end state.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology across all 4 nodes: node1=VyOS (eth0 default net DHCP client, eth1 private net), node2/node3=Ubuntu 24.04 (enp1s0 default net, enp8s0 private net), node4=Ubuntu 24.04 with ansible-core 2.20.5 pre-installed and no private-network NIC (the designated control_node)
Captured pre-change baseline: node1 eth1 unconfigured with no dhcp-server config in /config/config.boot; node2/node3 enp8s0 had no address

Bootstrapped SSH connectivity: generated missing sshd host keys and enabled+started ssh.service on node2/node3 (sshd was crash-looping due to absent host keys); added node4's pubkey to vyos user (node1) and root (node2/node3) authorized_keys

Discovered VyOS DHCP-server config schema differs from generic examples for this VyOS rolling release (needed subnet-id, range <tag> start/stop, option default-router/name-server nested under 'option') by inspecting /opt/vyatta/share/vyatta-cfg/templates

Wrote Ansible inventory (vyos_router / dhcp_clients groups) and a two-play site.yml on node4: play 1 configures node1's eth1 static router address (10.50.50.254/24) and Kea DHCPv4 server (pool 10.50.50.100-200) via VyOS configure/commit/save; play 2 installs an explicit systemd-networkd DHCP=yes unit for enp8s0 on node2/node3, reloads networkd, and renews the DHCP lease

Ran ansible-playbook; fixed an invalid config schema, re-ran successfully: node2 leased 10.50.50.100, node3 leased 10.50.50.101, both confirmed via systemd-networkd DHCPv4 acquisition logs and ping from node1

Fixed authorized_keys being wiped by VyOS's system_login.py reconciler on reboot by re-adding the SSH key through 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' (VyOS's own config language) instead of direct file edit

Executed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline on all 4 nodes, restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot, polled each until exec was available again, and proved boot_id changed for every node

Verified post-restart recovery: node1 retained its eth1 address and dhcp-server config with Kea DHCPv4 service active, and could ping both clients; node2 and node3 re-acquired their identical DHCP leases (10.50.50.100 / 10.50.50.101) from node1 after their own reboots
Ran the full Ansible playbook once more after all four restarts to confirm idempotency (node1 reported no configuration changes) and correctness of the final state

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DHCP server on private network shared with node2/node3
evidence.summary: VyOS dhcp-server config committed to /config/config.boot for shared-network LAN on 10.50.50.0/24, and isc-kea-dhcp4-server.service confirmed active; applied via the Ansible playbook's vyos_router play

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 obtain address via DHCP from node1 instead of static
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no static config/address on enp8s0; Ansible dhcp_clients play installed a DHCP=yes systemd-networkd unit and both nodes acquired dynamic leases 10.50.50.100/10.50.50.101 confirmed via ip addr and networkctl status logs

All configuration applied via ansible-playbook run from node4 (the ansible-core-equipped control_node) against an inventory of node1 (vyos_router) and node2/node3 (dhcp_clients), with a final idempotent re-run confirming correctness

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9028a473; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id fca1196c (changed); eth1 address, Kea service active, and ping connectivity to both DHCP clients all confirmed recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bfd05127; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 7f4bdffc (changed); enp8s0 re-acquired the same DHCP lease 10.50.50.100 from node1, confirmed via systemd-networkd log

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 63f96994; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 5f55fe43 (changed); enp8s0 re-acquired the same DHCP lease 10.50.50.101 from node1, confirmed via systemd-networkd log

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a6937a34; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 76035a72 (changed); recovered state proven by successfully re-running the full Ansible playbook from node4 afterward (control-node tooling and SSH keys intact)
